 It’s Election Day! BernCo is Ready for Voters
 Nov. 3, 2026 
 Bernalillo County – Polls are open for the 2026 General Election, with 74 voting locations throughout Bernalillo County welcoming voters from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters may cast their ballots at any location in the county, and Same-Day Registration is available at all locations.
 “ Election Day is here, and our election team is ready to serve voters across Bernalillo County ,” says Bernalillo County Clerk Michelle S. Kavanaugh. “ We encourage everyone to find a convenient voting location, allow enough time and remember that if you’re in line by 7 p.m., you will be able to vote .”
 Voting Locations and Wait Times 
 All voting locations in Bernalillo County are Voting Convenience Centers, meaning voters are not assigned to a specific location. Some locations may be busier than others, particularly during peak voting hours. Voters are encouraged to consider another location if their preferred site is busy.
 Find a Voting Location: 
 https://www.berncoclerk.gov/elections/election-day-voting/ 
 Voters who are in line by 7 p.m. will be allowed to cast their ballots.
 Same-Day Registration 
 Eligible voters who need to register or update their voter registration may do so at any Election Day voting location and cast a ballot during the same visit. Identification required by New Mexico law must be provided to complete Same-Day Registration.
 Returning Absentee Ballots 
 Voters who have not yet returned their completed absentee ballots must do so by 7 p.m. today . Ballots may be hand-delivered to any voting location or official election drop box.
 Voters can check the status of their absentee ballot at NMVote.gov.
 Election Night Results 
 Election Night results are unofficial. Initial results will be released after the polls close and the last voter has cast a ballot. Additional results will be reported as they become available.  
 Official results are determined following the completion and certification of the canvass.
 For voting locations, absentee ballot dropbox locations, and additional information about voting in Bernalillo County, visit BerncoClerk.gov, call (505) 243-VOTE (8683), or email clerk@bernco.gov .
 # # #
 About Bernalillo County 
 Bernalillo County is 1,160 square miles and is New Mexico’s most populous county with more than 676,000 residents. Bernalillo County government provides a wide range of public services to residents who live in Albuquerque, Los Ranchos and Tijeras with approximately 106,000 residents living in unincorporated areas of the county. Bernalillo County employs approximately 2,800 people and has an annual operating budget, capital investments and other funds of more than $1 billion. Elected officials include five county commissioners, assessor, clerk, probate judge, sheriff and treasurer.
